problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $6y+9{y}^{″}=0.$  Find $f(n),$ given that the recurrence relation for ${a}_{n}$ can be written as

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{f(n)},\,n=0,1,2,…
$$
worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we find ${y}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
6{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+9{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}=0
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the second sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-2.$ This gives

$$
6{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+9{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+2)(m+1){a}_{m+2}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the second summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
6{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+9{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[6{a}_{n}+9(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
6{a}_{n}+9(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}=0.
$$

Finally, the recursion formula is

$$
{a}_{n+2}=-\frac{2{a}_{n}}{3(n+1)(n+2)},\,n=0,1,2,…
$$

Therefore, $f(n)=-\frac{3(n+1)(n+2)}{2}.$
